metadata.title: Frank Turek vs Christopher Hitchens: What Best Explains Reality?
metadata.label: Reality, theism, and atheism
metadata.motion: What best explains reality: theism, with a personal creator and revelation, or atheism, with no supernatural dimension?
metadata.sourceNote: Assessment based exclusively on the complete locally cached YouTube caption transcript and timestamped events (transcript SHA-256 1a9f4911928cf2c4ac3e673ea195a581fc8a1eda3d63deb44082c1b65ebcc394). Required below-high-confidence audio checks were completed before adjudication; representative quotations must be exact strings from quote-eligible locked source spans.
metadata.scoringNote: Scores are AI-generated estimates of argumentative performance under the locked adjudicated-consensus workflow. Repository code calculated every move, section, and overall result once, only after two isolated judgments, required audio review, and disputed-field adjudication closed.

routes.description: Establish that a personal creator and revelation provide a unified explanation for the universe’s existence and order, biological information, objective morality and reason, and historically grounded supernatural disclosure.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the cited features of reality require or are best unified by a transcendent personal cause, atheistic naturalism lacks comparable foundations for them, and evidence independently bridges generic theism to credible revelation.

motionBridge.description: Show that personal-creator theism with revelation explains the principal features of reality more adequately than a reality containing no supernatural dimension.

centralBridges.description: Establish that the finite physical universe requires an eternal, nonphysical, purposive cause capable of initiating spacetime.
Connect life-permitting cosmic conditions and biological information to intelligence rather than unguided natural processes.
Ground objective moral obligation, truth, logic, rational cognition, and scientific intelligibility in a transcendent mind.
Supply independent historical and epistemic grounds for moving from generic creator theism to personal action and credible revelation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Show that cosmic decay, suffering, and religious wrongdoing do not by themselves defeat purposeful creation or the truth of theism.
Require the atheistic alternative to account positively for the same cosmological, biological, moral, and rational data.

routes.description: Establish that natural processes and human social, psychological, and historical development explain the relevant features of reality without a supernatural hypothesis, while creator and revelation claims introduce unsupported inferences and additional difficulties.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalistic accounts remain sufficient without complete ultimate knowledge, the move from physical origins to a personal revealed deity is unwarranted, and observed suffering, religious diversity, and unreliable miracle traditions favor human and natural explanations.

motionBridge.description: Show that no supernatural dimension is needed to explain reality and that adding a personal creator and revelation yields no superior comparative explanation.

centralBridges.description: Separate scientific uncertainty about ultimate origins from evidence for a creator and show that physical explanations do not require a divine assumption.
Explain apparent biological design and human experience through evolution, physical processes, and other natural mechanisms.
Account for moral knowledge and responsibility through human solidarity, law, and social life without supernatural command or enforcement.
Explain religions and revelation claims as diverse human products while challenging miracle testimony and exclusive doctrinal authority.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test claims of competent benevolent design against cosmic waste, extinction, disease, prolonged suffering, and delayed revelation.
Assess whether doctrines of unaccountable divine authority generate coercion or violence rather than necessary moral guidance.

sections.title: Cosmic Origin and the Necessity of a Creator
sections.rationale: This issue bears directly on whether the universe’s finite existence requires a personal transcendent cause or whether physical explanation can remain adequate while ultimate origins are uncertain.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Biological Information, and Natural Order
sections.rationale: This section tests the competing explanatory inferences from life-permitting conditions and biological complexity to intelligence, evolution, or other unguided natural processes.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Divine Authority, and Human Solidarity
sections.rationale: The clash determines whether objective obligation requires a divine standard or whether moral knowledge, responsibility, and criticism can be grounded in human social existence.

sections.title: Reason, Truth, and Experience under Naturalism
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether logic, rational cognition, science, love, and transcendence require an immaterial theistic foundation or remain intelligible within naturalism.

sections.title: Revelation, Miracles, and the Human Origins of Religion
sections.rationale: This section governs the necessary bridge from generic creator claims to personal revelation by testing miracle evidence, scriptural reliability, religious diversity, and naturalistic accounts of belief.
